# Atlas ERP Audit — Structural / Performance / Convention Findings

I read the four governance docs (`STRUCTURE.md`, `PERFORMANCE.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `GITHUB-WORKFLOW.md`) plus relevant `DECISIONS.md` entries, then grepped codebase-wide and **read the actual code** behind every candidate before reporting. **Headline:** the codebase is unusually disciplined. File-size cap (clean — largest are 399), pagination machinery (keyset, default 50/max 200), error envelope (no raw `HTTPException`/dict in routers), idempotency on posting endpoints, index discipline (234 indexes; every hot FK/filter column I spot-checked is indexed), no orphan files, no `supplier` drift — all hold up. Findings below are mostly **minor** tech-debt; two perf items are the substantive ones.

---

## Category A — Performance (PERFORMANCE.md)

### A1. N+1 query loop in stock-count variance preview (read endpoint)
- **Severity:** major · **Label:** tech-debt; module:inventory
- **File:** `backend/app/modules/inventory/service/count_reads.py:159-182` (endpoint `GET /api/v1/inventory/stock-counts/{count_id}/variance-preview`, `count_router.py:145-155`)
- **What's wrong:** `variance_preview` loads **all** count lines, then loops issuing per-line `current_system_qty()` (1 query) + `queries.current_unit_cost()` (1-2 queries). That's 2-3 queries × N lines on a request-path read. The docstring itself admits "per-line a quant read + a unit-cost read." A physical inventory count routinely has thousands of lines. PERFORMANCE §2 rates lazy-per-row in a serialization loop `severity:major`; this is explicit per-row querying, and the endpoint is also unpaginated (it builds a preview line for every row).
- **Evidence:** `for line in lines:` at line 159 with two `await` DB calls inside; `current_unit_cost` (`queries.py:360`) is itself 1-2 queries.
- **Proposed fix:** bulk-load all live quants for the count's `(item_id, bin_id, lot_id)` set in one query, and unit costs for the distinct `item_id`s in one query (mirror the `require_postable_accounts` bulk pattern), then compute in Python. Paginate the line output.

### A2. N+1 dimension validation on the journal-posting path
- **Severity:** minor (major under heavy distribution entries) · **Label:** tech-debt; module:finance
- **File:** `backend/app/modules/finance/service/journal_validate.py:80-86` and `90-96` (`require_dimensions`)
- **What's wrong:** loops over distinct `cost_center_id`s and distinct `profit_center_id`s, issuing one `SELECT` per id (`queries.cost_center_exists` / `profit_center_exists`). The docstring concedes "One query per dimension over the distinct referenced ids." This is inconsistent with `require_postable_accounts` **in the same file** (lines 44-50), which does the correct single `WHERE id IN (...)` bulk query. Allocation/distribution journal entries can carry many distinct dimensions.
- **Proposed fix:** replace each loop with one `SELECT id WHERE tenant_id=? AND id IN (:ids)` per dimension type; diff against the requested set for the missing-id error (exactly the account pattern already used above it).

### A3. N+1 per-item read in the MRP demand build
- **Severity:** minor · **Label:** tech-debt; module:manufacturing
- **File:** `backend/app/modules/manufacturing/service/mrp.py:125-132` (`_open_sales_demand_items`)
- **What's wrong:** after one discovery query for demanded item ids, it calls `sales_queries.committed_quantity()` once **per item**. The docstring calls this "bounded," but it's O(n) in demanded items — exactly the per-row pattern PERFORMANCE §2 bans for bulk runs ("never per-row ORM loops over large sets"). MRP is backgrounded (D-026), so not latency-critical, but still a run-path N+1.
- **Proposed fix:** add a `sales/queries.committed_quantities(item_ids)` returning a `{item_id: qty}` map via one grouped query; consume it in the loop.

### A4. Leave-accrual run executes inline with no size threshold
- **Severity:** minor · **Label:** tech-debt; module:hr
- **File:** `backend/app/modules/hr/service/leave_accrual.py` (`accrue_leave`) via `hr/leave_router.py` `run_accrual`
- **What's wrong:** reads are bulk (3 queries — good), but the run materializes/inserts one `LeaveBalance` per (active employee × active leave type) inline in the request. For a volume tenant (thousands of employees) this is large in-request work. Unlike the established threshold pattern — depreciation routes >100 assets to a job (D-034), bank import >1k lines backgrounds (#26) — accrual has **no** job-routing threshold. The reorder-scan/preventive-maintenance "INLINE at v1 scale" note is referenced but accrual scales with headcount, not a small plan count.
- **Proposed fix:** route accrual to the `core/jobs.py` framework above an active-employee threshold (the depreciation `>100` precedent), returning 202 + job id.

*(Checked and clean: report CSV export streams (no in-memory materialization), `run_report` caps at 10k rows, AR/AP aging and org-chart are single-query + Python assembly (no N+1), payment/FX-reval/MRP/depreciation/bank-import already backgrounded.)*

### A5. AR/AP aging reports have no row cap / streaming fallback (§3)
- **Severity:** minor (low confidence — defensible exception) · **Label:** tech-debt; module:finance
- **File:** `backend/app/modules/finance/service/ar_aging.py:48-61` (and `ap_aging.py` mirror); endpoint `ar_router.py:258`
- **What's wrong:** loads every open invoice for the tenant with no 10k cap / CSV-streaming path (PERFORMANCE §3). Single query, so no N+1; but a very large open-AR set materializes fully in memory.
- **Note:** aging must be complete per partner to be correct, so a hard row-cap would break it — this is a defensible deviation; flagging only for the §3 checklist. Lower priority.

---

## Category B — Structure / Dependency Rules (STRUCTURE §5)

### B1. Cross-module `constants.py` imports not on the §5 allowlist; one bidirectional pair
- **Severity:** minor · **Label:** tech-debt; module:core (isolation)
- **Files (representative):** `backend/app/modules/inventory/handlers.py:52,57,59,64` (imports `manufacturing/procurement/quality/sales` `.constants`); `backend/app/modules/manufacturing/service/production_post.py:46` (imports `inventory.constants`); plus reporting/finance handlers.
- **What's wrong:** STRUCTURE §5 names only `queries.py` and `events.py` as the files one module may import from another. The pervasive pattern of importing another module's `constants.py` (for docflow `*_LINK` link-type strings) is outside that allowlist. More notably, **inventory↔manufacturing is bidirectional** (`inventory/handlers.py` imports `manufacturing.constants`; `manufacturing/...production_post.py` imports `inventory.constants`), and §5 explicitly forbids bidirectional cross-module dependencies.
- **Evidence/mitigation:** confined to `handlers.py`/leaf service files (not `__init__`), constants are literal-only, so there's no runtime import cycle or logic coupling — the spirit of §5 holds; only the letter (allowlist + bidirectional rule) is violated.
- **Proposed fix:** either (a) record a DECISIONS entry adding `constants.py` to the §5 importable set (it's data-only), or (b) move shared docflow link-type constants used by subscribers into the publishing module's `events.py` (already importable) so handlers import them from there.

*(Checked and OK: `core/bootstrap.py` importing module routers/events is the sanctioned app-wiring file; `core/security_router.py`→`admin.service` is documented D-008; `reporting/report_registry.py` model imports are the documented D-059 whitelist exception; `finance/handlers/payroll.py`→`hr.models` is a documented lazy-import. None are reported as defects.)*

---

## Category C — Terminology Lock (STRUCTURE §7)

### C1. "product" used as a canonical identifier in the margin report (should be "item")
- **Severity:** minor · **Label:** tech-debt; module:finance
- **Files:** `backend/app/modules/finance/statements_router.py:109` (route `/margin-by-product`), `statements_schemas.py:144` (`class MarginByProductRead`), `service/statements/margin.py:1,46,57` (`class MarginByProduct`, `def margin_by_product`), re-exported in `service/__init__.py:134,246` and `statements/__init__.py`.
- **What's wrong:** the report groups by the journal's **`item_id`** dimension — its own docstring says "per item" / "the journal's `item_id` dimension" — yet the public API route, response schema, service class, and function name all use **"product."** STRUCTURE §7 / CLAUDE.md lock the canonical term to `item` (not product/sku/article), and this is an internal name, not an industry display-label override. Not recorded as an intentional choice in DECISIONS.
- **Proposed fix:** rename to `margin-by-item` / `MarginByItemRead` / `MarginByItem` / `margin_by_item` (a rename-only commit per STRUCTURE §8.10).

*(Other "product"/"sku" hits are docstrings/comments — mathematical "product", CRM "expected products", S/4 parity notes, `vendor_item_code` — not identifier drift. No `supplier` drift in code.)*

---

## Category D — Idempotency (CLAUDE.md / D-013)

### D1. Draft `create_customer_invoice` / `create_vendor_bill` register a document but accept no idempotency key
- **Severity:** minor (medium confidence it's a defect vs. intentional) · **Label:** tech-debt; module:finance
- **Files:** `backend/app/modules/finance/ar_router.py` `create_customer_invoice`; `ap_router.py` `create_vendor_bill`. Both services call `docflow.register_document(...)` at draft creation (`service/customer_invoices.py:169`), and the models carry `DocumentMixin` (`models/receivables.py:46`, `models/payables.py:41`).
- **What's wrong:** D-013 requires an idempotency key on "every financial/stock-document endpoint." These two `create_*` endpoints **register a `core_documents` row** (a document), so a double-submit creates two distinct draft invoice/bill documents — yet they have no key, while their siblings that also create documents (`create_customer_receipt`, `create_vendor_payment`, `create_goods_receipt`, `create_delivery`, `create_stock_move`, `create_sales_order`, `create_billing`, `create_return`, `create_invoice_match`, `create_purchase_order`, `create_quote`, etc.) all do.
- **Mitigation:** the `ar_router.py` docstring (lines 8-9) states the intent — only "post invoice" is treated as the financial-document endpoint (the gapless number + journal are claimed at POST per D-012/D-017), and `/post` IS idempotent. So a duplicate draft has no financial/stock effect. This makes it a **consistency gap** more than a money-integrity bug — hence minor, and possibly an intentional (if under-documented) choice.
- **Proposed fix:** either add `Idempotent("finance.ar.invoice.create")` / `...bill.create` to the two draft creators for parity, or record the "draft-create is not a document endpoint" rule explicitly in D-013/DECISIONS so the distinction is intentional and auditable.

async def _reverse_previous_run(
    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, period: FiscalPeriod, next_start: date
) -> None:
    """Reverse a prior COMPLETED run's entries before reposting (D-019 re-run rule: append-only,
    never delete). Every prior FX_REVAL entry that is still POSTED and is not itself a reversal is
    reversed into its own period (period-dated adjustments into the revalued period, next-period
    auto-reversals into the next period), and the prior run row(s) are marked REVERSED. Reversing
    both halves nets the prior run fully out so the fresh run starts clean."""
    prior_runs = (
        await session.execute(
            select(FxRevaluationRun).where(
                FxRevaluationRun.tenant_id == tenant_id,
                FxRevaluationRun.fiscal_period_id == period.id,
                FxRevaluationRun.status == FxRunStatus.COMPLETED.value,
            )
        )
    ).scalars().all()
    if not prior_runs:
        return
    prior_entries = (
        await session.execute(
            select(JournalEntry).where(
                JournalEntry.tenant_id == tenant_id,
                JournalEntry.document_type == DocumentType.FX_REVAL.value,
                JournalEntry.status == EntryStatus.POSTED.value,
                JournalEntry.reverses_entry_id.is_(None),
            )
        )
    ).scalars().all()
    for entry in prior_entries:
        in_revalued_period = period.start_date <= entry.posting_date <= period.end_date
        reversal_date = entry.posting_date if in_revalued_period else next_start
        await reverse_entry(
            session,
            tenant_id,
            entry.id,
            reversal_date,
            description=f"Re-run reversal of {entry.entry_number or entry.id}",
        )
    for run in prior_runs:
        run.status = FxRunStatus.REVERSED.value
    await session.flush()


async def run_fx_revaluation(
    session: AsyncSession,
    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
    period_id: uuid.UUID,
    rate_date: date,
) -> FxRevaluationRun:
    """Run unrealized-FX revaluation for ``period_id`` at ``rate_date`` (D-019).

    1. Resolve the functional currency (422 if unconfigured) and validate the period exists.
    2. Validate the NEXT period exists and is OPEN up front (the auto-reversal posts there) — a
       clear 422 BEFORE any entry posts.
    3. If a prior COMPLETED run exists for this period, reverse its entries first (append-only).
    4. For each monetary foreign account with a non-zero foreign balance as of ``rate_date``:
       delta = quantize(foreign_balance × CLOSING_rate, functional_decimals) − functional carrying.
       Post ONE balanced FX_REVAL adjustment (adjustment vs fx_unrealized_gain/loss) plus its
       next-period auto-reversal, linked 'revalues'.
    5. Record the run COMPLETED. The caller commits via run_in_uow.
    """
    functional_code = await fx.functional_currency(session, tenant_id)
    period = await session.get(FiscalPeriod, period_id)

        tenant_id=tenant_id,
        fiscal_period_id=period_id,
        rate_date=rate_date,

"""Runtime settings, env-prefixed ATLAS_; field names mirror .env.example exactly."""

from functools import lru_cache
from typing import Annotated

from pydantic import field_validator
from pydantic_settings import BaseSettings, NoDecode, SettingsConfigDict


class Settings(BaseSettings):
    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(env_prefix="ATLAS_", env_file=".env", extra="ignore")

    env: str = "dev"
    # SQLite default so the app boots with zero configuration; Postgres via .env.
    database_url: str = "sqlite+aiosqlite:///./atlas.db"
    jwt_secret: str = "change-me"
    jwt_access_ttl_seconds: int = 900
    jwt_refresh_ttl_seconds: int = 1209600
    # NoDecode: pydantic-settings would otherwise JSON-decode list fields before
    # validators run; the env var is a plain comma-separated string.
    cors_origins: Annotated[list[str], NoDecode] = ["http://localhost:5173"]
    log_level: str = "INFO"
    # D-010 audit context: honor the left-most X-Forwarded-For hop ONLY when the app
    # sits behind a trusted proxy. Default false — read request.client.host directly so
    # a client can never spoof its audited IP by sending the header itself.
    trust_proxy: bool = False

    @field_validator("cors_origins", mode="before")
    @classmethod
    def _split_comma_separated(cls, value: object) -> object:
        if isinstance(value, str):
            return [origin.strip() for origin in value.split(",") if origin.strip()]
        return value


@lru_cache
def get_settings() -> Settings:
    return Settings()

cd "/Users/taha/Claude projects/expremental ERP/atlas-erp" && gh issue create --repo Taha-Mahmoodi/atlas-erp \
  --title "FX revaluation re-run reverses every period's FX_REVAL entries, not just the re-run period" \
  --label "found-during-build,bug,module:finance,severity:major" \
  --body-file - <<'EOF'
_Found during a full read-through audit of the committed backend (Phases 0–13); verified against source._

**What's wrong**
`_reverse_previous_run` in `backend/app/modules/finance/service/fx_revaluation.py:218-259` is meant to reverse only the prior run's entries for the period being re-run. The `prior_runs` probe (lines 226-234) is correctly period-scoped (`fiscal_period_id == period.id`), but the `prior_entries` query that actually drives the `reverse_entry` calls (lines 237-246) has **no period/date/run scope** — it matches every still-posted FX_REVAL entry tenant-wide:

```python
select(JournalEntry).where(
    JournalEntry.tenant_id == tenant_id,
    JournalEntry.document_type == DocumentType.FX_REVAL.value,
    JournalEntry.status == EntryStatus.POSTED.value,
    JournalEntry.reverses_entry_id.is_(None),
)
```

So re-running one period reverses the active FX_REVAL adjustments/auto-reversals of **all other periods** too, while only the re-run period's run row is flipped to `REVERSED` (lines 257-258). The run rows and the GL entries go out of sync; the model docstring (`models/fx.py:130-136`) promises the run's entries are scoped via the `'revalues'` docflow edges, but those edges are never consulted.

**Reproduction**
1. Post a foreign-currency monetary balance.
2. Run revaluation for period **March** (rate 3/31) and **April** (rate 4/30) → 4 active FX_REVAL entries.
3. Re-run **March only**. Result: April's 4/30 adjustment and 5/1 auto-reversal are also reversed, even though April was never re-run; April's run row still reads `COMPLETED`. April's balance-sheet revaluation silently disappears. (If April is closed, the spurious reversal trips the closed-period trigger and the entire March re-run rolls back with a misleading `finance.period_closed`.) Existing test `test_rerun_reverses_prior_then_reposts` only re-runs the same period, so it never exercises this.

**Impact**
Silently corrupts already-posted, balanced FX revaluations in untouched periods → wrong balance sheet / unrealized-FX figures. Financial-integrity defect on the universal journal.

**Proposed fix**
Scope `prior_entries` to the run(s) being reversed: follow the `'revalues'` docflow edges from `prior_runs`, or add an `fx_revaluation_run_id` FK on the entries and reverse only that run's entries (and bound by `period.start_date..end_date`).
EOF

_Found during a full read-through audit of the committed backend (Phases 0–13); verified against source._

**What's wrong**
`create_fiscal_year` (`backend/app/modules/finance/service/periods.py:65-111`) validates only that the year **code** is unique (lines 71-83). It does not check the new year's `[start_date, end_date]` against existing years, and migration 0008 has no DB-level guard against overlap (only per-row `start_date <= end_date` CHECKs and a `(tenant_id, fiscal_year_id, period_number)` UNIQUE). `find_period_for_date` (`backend/app/modules/finance/queries/periods.py:30-35`) then does `scalar_one_or_none()` over the matching periods — its docstring assumes "at most one matches," but that only holds *within* a year, not across overlapping years.

**Reproduction**
1. Create FY `2026`, start 2026-01-01, 12 periods (ends 2026-12-31).
2. Create FY `2026H2`, start 2026-06-01.
3. Post a journal entry dated 2026-07-15 → `find_period_for_date` matches two periods → `sqlalchemy ... MultipleResultsFound` → unhandled **HTTP 500**. `get_period_status` (same lookup) breaks identically. Current tests only cover contiguity within a single year.

**Impact**
An admin misconfiguration makes every posting dated in the overlap window crash with a 500 instead of a clear 422; the date→period lookup is on the journal posting hot path.

**Proposed fix**
In `create_fiscal_year`, reject when `[start_date, year_end]` intersects any existing year's range for the tenant (one indexed query) with a clear 422. Optionally make `find_period_for_date` defensive (order + `first()`), but the real fix is preventing the overlap.
EOF

  --title "Receipt/payment amount isn't validated against the allocation sum → same-currency over/under-payment misbooked as realized FX" \
  --label "found-during-build,bug,module:finance,severity:major" \
  --body-file - <<'EOF'
_Found during a full read-through audit of the committed backend (Phases 0–13); verified against source._

**What's wrong**
`_validate_allocations` in `backend/app/modules/finance/service/customer_receipts.py:62-114` (and the AP mirror in `vendor_payments.py`) checks each allocation is positive and ≤ the invoice's open amount, but **never checks `sum(allocations) == receipt_amount`**. The cash/bank side (`payload.amount`, line 182) and the control side (`Σ allocations`) then flow independently into `clearing_fx._fx_line` (`backend/app/modules/finance/service/clearing_fx.py:176-210`), which books their functional difference to the realized FX gain/loss account. For a **same-currency** receipt/payment (no conversion), that difference is pure over/under-payment, not FX — yet it is posted as a phantom FX gain/loss. The entry still balances, so it posts successfully.

**Reproduction**
`create_and_post_receipt(amount=110.00, allocations=[(invoice, 100.00)])` with invoice currency == functional currency. Posts: Dr bank 110 / Cr AR 100 / Cr "Realized FX gain" 10. The 10 overpayment is misclassified as an FX gain instead of unapplied cash / customer credit. Same on AP with `amount < Σ allocations` → phantom FX loss. Every existing test happens to pass `amount == Σ allocations`, so this is unproven.

**Impact**
Misstates realized-FX P&L and leaves AR/AP not reflecting unapplied cash; a data-entry mismatch silently lands in the wrong GL account. Financial-correctness defect.

**Proposed fix**
In `create_and_post_payment` / `create_and_post_receipt`, validate `quantize(payload.amount) == Σ allocation amounts` and raise 422 on mismatch — or explicitly model over/under-payment as unapplied cash — before building the clearing entry.

  --body-file - <<'EOF'
_Found during a full read-through audit of the committed backend (Phases 0–13); verified against source._

**What's wrong**
`_validate_match_line` in `backend/app/modules/procurement/service/invoice_matches.py:150-183` computes the quantity variance against the **remaining-to-bill** quantity instead of against the received/expected quantity:

```python
open_to_bill = received_quantity - billed_quantity          # line 151
# over-billing already guarded: qty <= open_to_bill          # line 152
quantity_variance = qty - open_to_bill                       # line 174  → always <= 0
qty_pct = abs(quantity_variance) / open_to_bill * 100        # line 180-182
```

Because the over-billing guard caps `qty <= open_to_bill`, `quantity_variance` is always ≤ 0. Any invoice for *less* than the full open quantity — a normal partial invoice — yields a large `qty_pct`, and with the default 0% quantity tolerance (`DEFAULT_QUANTITY_TOLERANCE_PERCENT = 0`, `constants.py:187`) the line is `within_tolerance = False`, forcing the whole match to `EXCEPTION`. An EXCEPTION can't post without a manual override (`invoice_match_post.py:101-106`). A supplied `goods_receipt_line_id` is ignored by the variance math entirely.

**Reproduction**
PO line ordered 10 / received 10 / billed 0 / cost 5. Create a match line `matched_quantity=4`, `unit_price=5` (0 price variance) → `open_to_bill=10`, `quantity_variance=-6`, `qty_pct=60%` → `within_tolerance=False` → status **EXCEPTION**. Tests only ever bill the full quantity, so this is uncovered. Contradicts the parity doc's "Full" 3-way match (partial receipts/bills reconcile).

**Impact**
Partial vendor invoicing — a routine P2P workflow — is impossible without a manual override on every partial bill.

**Proposed fix**
Compute quantity variance as invoiced-vs-received for *this* match: when a `goods_receipt_line_id` is supplied, base expected qty on that GR line; otherwise treat an at-or-below-open partial as zero quantity variance and only flag when invoiced **exceeds** the received quantity.
EOF

  --label "found-during-build,bug,module:sales,severity:major" \
  --body-file - <<'EOF'
_Found during a full read-through audit of the committed backend (Phases 0–13); verified against source._

**What's wrong**
The over-fulfillment guard lives only in the **create** path and compares the requested qty against the *currently persisted* fulfilled column — which isn't raised until **post**. The post path then blindly increments with no cap re-check:
- Deliveries: create check `deliveries.py:110-123` (`qty > ordered − delivered_quantity`); post `delivery_post.py:76-80` does `order_line.delivered_quantity = delivered_quantity + line.quantity` with no cap.
- Billing: `billing.py:162-175` vs `billing_post.py:136-156` (same pattern, `invoiced_quantity`).
- Returns: `returns.py:118-131` vs `returns_post.py:105-109` (`returned_quantity`).
- No DB backstop: `0029_sales_orders.py:186-193` gives `delivered_quantity`/`invoiced_quantity` only `server_default="0"`, no `<= ordered` CHECK.

So two DRAFT documents created before either posts both pass the create check (column still at the old value), and posting both over-fulfills. The only post-time backstop for deliveries is `InsufficientStockError`, which fires only when stock is exhausted — not when the ordered qty is exceeded with ample stock; billing and returns have no backstop at all.

**Reproduction**
Order line ordered=100, delivered=0. Create DRAFT delivery D1 qty 100 (open=100, passes) and DRAFT delivery D2 qty 100 (delivered still 0, open=100, passes). Post D1 → delivered=100. Post D2 → delivered=200, no rejection (ample stock). Same sequence over-bills and over-returns.

**Impact**
Violates "can't over-deliver beyond ordered" / "can't return more than delivered" — over-ships stock, over-invoices revenue/AR, over-credits returns. Reachable in any normal multi-step or concurrent workflow.

**Proposed fix**
Re-validate `delivered/invoiced/returned + line.quantity <= ordered/delivered/invoiced` inside the post path (the `_advance.../_raise...` loops), failing the post if exceeded; add portable DB CHECK constraints as a backstop.
EOF

cd "/Users/taha/Claude projects/expremental ERP/atlas-erp" && gh issue create --repo Taha-Mahmoodi/atlas-erp \
  --title "MRP drops dependent demand for shared/diamond components already netted at an earlier level" \
  --label "found-during-build,bug,module:manufacturing,severity:major" \
  --body-file - <<'EOF'
_Found during a full read-through audit of the committed backend (Phases 0–13); verified against source._

**What's wrong**
`_plan_levels` in `backend/app/modules/manufacturing/service/mrp.py:203-259` nets each item exactly once, at the first level it appears, and adds it to `netted` (line 232). At each deeper level it filters `item_ids = [i for i in pending if i not in netted]` (line 220). When a component appears as *dependent* demand at a deeper level but was *already* netted earlier (independent reorder demand, or a diamond BOM where a component is shared by two parents at different levels), its deeper dependent demand sits in `pending`/`next_pending` but is filtered out — so that demand is **never added to any planned-order quantity**. The docstring (lines 214-216) claims this case is "folded into its earlier net rather than re-planned (low-level-code)," but the code does not fold — it drops. Real MRP solves this with low-level codes: gather all gross demand for an item before netting it.

**Reproduction**
BOM: Finished F → Sub S (×2) + Raw R1 (×3); Sub S → Raw R2 (×4). Sales demand F=10 **and** R1 independently demanded 50 (reorder point). Correct R1 plan = 50 + (3×10) = **80**. The algorithm nets R1 at level 0 only → plans **50**; the 30 dependent units from F's explosion are dropped. (Confirmed by simulating the exact loop. `test_mrp.py` / `test_mrp_planning.py` only exercise a clean tree where each raw is used by a single parent, so the bug is uncovered.)

**Impact**
MRP under-plans any component with both independent and dependent demand, or shared across BOM levels → material shortfalls. Violates "MRP nets demand vs supply correctly / correct planned-order qty."

**Proposed fix**
Compute each item's low-level code and net it only after all parents have contributed its full gross demand (accumulate gross demand per item across all levels before netting), instead of netting on first encounter.
EOF

_Found during a full read-through audit of the committed backend (Phases 0–13); verified against source._

**What's wrong**
`Settings.jwt_secret` defaults to the literal `"change-me"` and `env` defaults to `"dev"` (`backend/app/core/config.py:13-16`). Nothing validates that a real secret is set when running in production — there is no `@field_validator` for `jwt_secret`, no `create_app` startup check, no fail-on-default (the only validator there is for `cors_origins`). The app boots and signs/verifies JWTs with `change-me` (`auth.py:79-80,129`) if the operator forgets `ATLAS_JWT_SECRET`. Because the repo is public, anyone knowing the default can forge a valid token for any `sub`/`tenant_id`.

**Reproduction**
Deploy without `ATLAS_JWT_SECRET`. Forge `jwt.encode({"sub": <any user id>, "tenant_id": <target tenant>, "sid": ..., "ver": 0, "typ": "access", "iat":..., "exp":...}, "change-me", "HS256")`. `get_current_user` accepts it; `current_tenant_id` is set from the forged claim → full auth bypass and cross-tenant access.

**Impact**
A single missing env var silently ships an authentication-bypass / cross-tenant-isolation hole. Defense-in-depth gap on the auth invariant.

**Proposed fix**
Add a validator (or `create_app` check) that raises at startup if `env in {"prod","production"}` and `jwt_secret == "change-me"` (or is shorter than ~32 chars). Document the requirement in `.env.example`.
EOF

Malformed input the parser claims to validate crashes with a 500 (minor robustness/contract defect).

**Proposed fix**
In `_row_problem`, after parsing, reject non-finite values: `if not amount.is_finite(): return f"amount {raw_amount!r} is not a finite number"`.

_Found during a full read-through audit of the committed backend (Phases 0–13); verified against source._

**What's wrong**
`_apply_transfer` (MAV branch, `backend/app/modules/inventory/service/costing.py:301-308`) issues from the source and receives into the destination at the same computed cost:

```python
cost, _residual = await costing_mav.mav_issue(... from_warehouse_id ...)   # residual discarded
unit_cost = (cost / qty) if qty > 0 else Decimal(0)
await costing_mav.mav_receive(... to_warehouse_id ..., qty, unit_cost)
```

`mav_issue` (`costing_mav.py:101-108`) flushes a residual `total_value − cogs` to zero when the source on-hand hits exactly 0, and returns it. `_apply_transfer` discards that residual (`_residual`) and moves only `cost` into the destination. So when a transfer empties the source and the average isn't exact, the source's leftover value vanishes (or an over-issue creates value): total inventory value across both warehouses changes by `residual`. A transfer publishes **no** `StockValued` event (net GL effect is intended to be zero), so nothing balances this drift — the GL inventory account silently diverges from `Σ inv_item_valuations.total_value`.

**Reproduction**
MAV item, warehouse A holds qty at a non-terminating average (e.g. total_value 10 / qty 3). Transfer all units A→B; `mav_issue` zeroes A and returns a nonzero quantize residual which is dropped; B receives only `cost`. Same-warehouse transfers (the only ones tested) never hit this branch.

**Impact**
Sub-cent-to-cent inventory valuation drift on cross-warehouse transfers that empty a source with an inexact average, with no offsetting journal. Accumulates over many transfers.

**Proposed fix**
Fold the issue residual into the destination receipt value (receive `cost + residual`, or add `residual` to the destination `total_value`) so total valuation is conserved across the two rows.
EOF

**What's wrong**
D-013 requires an idempotency key on "every financial/stock-document endpoint." `create_customer_invoice` (`ar_router.py`) and `create_vendor_bill` (`ap_router.py`) both call `docflow.register_document(...)` at draft creation (e.g. `service/customer_invoices.py:169`) and the models carry `DocumentMixin` (`models/receivables.py:46`, `models/payables.py:41`) — i.e. they create a `core_documents` row — yet neither accepts an idempotency key. Every sibling that also creates a document (`create_customer_receipt`, `create_vendor_payment`, `create_goods_receipt`, `create_delivery`, `create_stock_move`, `create_sales_order`, `create_billing`, `create_return`, `create_invoice_match`, `create_purchase_order`, `create_quote`, …) does have one. So a double-submit creates two distinct draft invoice/bill documents.

**Reproduction**
POST the same `create_customer_invoice` (or `create_vendor_bill`) payload twice → two draft documents/numbers; no dedupe.

**Impact**
Consistency gap, not a money-integrity bug: the gapless number + journal are claimed at POST (which *is* idempotent), so a duplicate draft has no financial/stock effect — but it diverges from the D-013 rule and the rest of the document-creating endpoints.

**Proposed fix**
Either add `Idempotent("finance.ar.invoice.create")` / `...bill.create` to the two draft creators for parity, or record explicitly in DECISIONS/D-013 that "draft create is not a document endpoint; the POST is" so the distinction is intentional and auditable.
EOF

## n8n
This is the official MCP server for n8n, a workflow automation platform.

This MCP server provides tools to build n8n workflows programmatically using the n8n Workflow SDK.

To build n8n workflows, follow these steps in order:

1. Read the SDK reference: You MUST call get_sdk_reference (or use the n8n://workflow-sdk/reference resource) before writing workflow code. Do not guess SDK syntax.

2. Get suggested nodes: You MUST call get_suggested_nodes with all relevant workflow technique categories before searching for nodes. Use the recommendations, pattern hints, and configuration guidance to decide which nodes and patterns to use.

3. Discover nodes: Call search_nodes with queries for services you need (e.g., ["gmail", "slack", "schedule trigger"]), utility nodes (e.g., ["set", "if", "merge", "code"]), and suggested nodes you plan to use. Note the discriminators (resource/operation/mode) in the results.

4. Get type definitions: Call get_node_types with ALL node IDs you plan to use, including discriminators from search results. This returns the exact TypeScript parameter definitions. DO NOT skip this — guessing parameter names creates invalid workflows.

5. Write the workflow code using the SDK patterns from the reference and the exact parameter names from the type definitions. Follow the coding guidelines and design guidance sections of the SDK reference (retrieve them with get_sdk_reference using sections "guidelines" and "design").

6. Validate: Call validate_workflow with your full code. Fix any errors and re-validate until valid.

7. Create: Call create_workflow_from_code with the validated code to save the workflow to n8n. Include a short `description` (1-2 sentences) summarizing what the workflow does — this helps users find and understand their workflows.

Done. Here's the full picture of the audit.

## What I did

I audited the **committed backend** (Phases 0–13: core platform through reporting — ~250 Python files, 42 migrations). Baseline was healthy: the suite is **green (1662 passed, 20 PG-only skips)** and the file-size caps hold, so the obvious surface is well covered. The real defects are in logic the tests don't exercise, so I did a deep read-through across every module (parallel domain audits, then I personally verified each finding against source before filing). I deliberately **excluded** the then-uncommitted `industry`/`admin` work (it has since merged as [PR #85](https://github.com/Taha-Mahmoodi/atlas-erp/pull/85), so Phase 14.1 now warrants its own pass).

Every issue follows the repo's §6 format (What's wrong / Reproduction / Impact / Proposed fix) with exact `file:line`, and carries `found-during-build` + `bug`/`tech-debt` + `module:*` + `severity:*`.

## 16 issues filed

**Major (8)** — financial/stock/auth correctness:
- [#71](https://github.com/Taha-Mahmoodi/atlas-erp/issues/71) FX revaluation re-run reverses **every** period's FX_REVAL entries, not just the re-run period *(two agents found this independently)*
- [#72](https://github.com/Taha-Mahmoodi/atlas-erp/issues/72) Overlapping fiscal years → posting in the overlap raises HTTP 500
- [#73](https://github.com/Taha-Mahmoodi/atlas-erp/issues/73) Receipt/payment amount not validated vs allocation sum → same-currency over/under-payment misbooked as realized FX
- [#74](https://github.com/Taha-Mahmoodi/atlas-erp/issues/74) 3-way match flags every legitimate **partial** invoice as a quantity-variance EXCEPTION
- [#75](https://github.com/Taha-Mahmoodi/atlas-erp/issues/75) Over-deliver/over-bill/over-return via multiple DRAFT documents (no post-time cap, no DB CHECK)
- [#76](https://github.com/Taha-Mahmoodi/atlas-erp/issues/76) MRP drops dependent demand for shared/diamond components (low-level-code bug)
- [#77](https://github.com/Taha-Mahmoodi/atlas-erp/issues/77) Default JWT secret `change-me` can ship to prod with no startup guard
- [#78](https://github.com/Taha-Mahmoodi/atlas-erp/issues/78) Stock-count variance-preview endpoint is N+1 and unpaginated

**Minor (8)** — robustness, perf, security hardening, convention:
- [#79](https://github.com/Taha-Mahmoodi/atlas-erp/issues/79) Bank CSV import accepts Infinity/NaN → 500 / misleading error
- [#80](https://github.com/Taha-Mahmoodi/atlas-erp/issues/80) Login is a user/tenant enumeration timing oracle
- [#81](https://github.com/Taha-Mahmoodi/atlas-erp/issues/81) `require_dimensions` N+1 on the journal-posting path (bulk pattern exists 30 lines above)
- [#82](https://github.com/Taha-Mahmoodi/atlas-erp/issues/82) Documented CI grep-gate banning raw `text()` doesn't exist — tenancy bypass seam unguarded
- [#83](https://github.com/Taha-Mahmoodi/atlas-erp/issues/83) Margin report uses "product" as a canonical identifier (terminology-lock violation)
- [#84](https://github.com/Taha-Mahmoodi/atlas-erp/issues/84) Cross-warehouse MAV transfer discards the rounding residual → valuation drifts from GL
- [#87](https://github.com/Taha-Mahmoodi/atlas-erp/issues/87) Counting an item up at zero book cost raises `receipt_unit_cost_required` and rolls back the count
- [#88](https://github.com/Taha-Mahmoodi/atlas-erp/issues/88) Draft invoice/bill creation registers a document but accepts no idempotency key (D-013 gap)

I also closed [#86](https://github.com/Taha-Mahmoodi/atlas-erp/issues/86) as a duplicate of #84 — the session was interrupted mid-filing and that one got created twice.

## Notes & judgment calls
- **The codebase is genuinely well-engineered.** Tenant isolation, the double-entry/immutability DB guards, the largest-remainder money allocator, auth rotation/revocation, idempotency races, keyset pagination, and HR field-masking all held up under scrutiny — the HR/CRM/reporting sweep found **nothing** (and cleared the `float(ratio)` you might worry about — it's an OTD *percentage*, not money).
- **#71 severity**: I rated it `major`; one reviewer argued `blocker`. It corrupts posted FX data across periods but doesn't unbalance the books, so I went major — easy to bump if you disagree.
- **Didn't file** (low value / defensible, mentioned for completeness): the inclusive-tax `calculate_document_tax` cent-drift (real but currently has no production caller), AR/AP aging having no row cap (aging must be complete to be correct — a defensible §3 deviation), and a few smaller minor-perf items (MRP demand-build N+1, leave-accrual inline threshold, cross-module `constants.py` imports). Happy to file any of these if you want them tracked.

Want me to start fixing any of these (the issue-first protocol points to `fix/<issue#>-<slug>` branches with a regression test), beginning with the majors?
